title: Microbially Fermented Agricultural Residues Supplemented with Chelates as Organic Fertilizers for Rice Production
content: Microbially fermented agricultural residues supplemented with chelated micronutrients may offer a locally produced fertilizer option for rice cultivation. This study developed liquid, concentrated organic fertilizers (COFs) from Azolla, fish meal, mung bean residue, coffee grounds, and ground chicken feathers via fermentation with fungal, bacterial, and actinomycete inoculants. Nutrient and heavy-metal concentrations were measured before and after fermentation was stopped. Nitrate levels declined by approximately half across all raw materials; phosphorus increased in fish meal, while potassium decreased markedly in coffee grounds and fish meal. Copper increased in most samples, selenium increased in all five, and cadmium rose in four, with fish meal showing the highest post-fermentation cadmium level; fish-meal-derived COF also had the highest phosphorus and calcium concentrations after fermentation was stopped. Two chelate formulations, CZB and Multi, were also developed, with nutrient concentrations close to their target levels. Four formulated COF treatments, with or without chelated micronutrients, were evaluated across four rice varieties in a field experiment using a split-plot randomized complete block design with three replications. Fertilizer treatment, rice variety, and their interaction significantly affected grain yield but not harvest age. Mean grain yield across treatments was 6,388 kg/ha. The Azolla- and fish-meal-derived fertilizer supplemented with chelate had the highest treatment mean yield (7,109 kg/ha), significantly exceeding that of the same organic fertilizer without chelate (5,579 kg/ha). Yield responses varied by variety: RD79 yielded most with the mung-bean-residue- and coffee-ground-derived fertilizer supplemented with chelate (9,305 kg/ha), whereas Hom Naka yielded most with chemical fertilizer (8,036 kg/ha). Harvest age ranged from 138 days in the no-fertilizer treatment to 148 days with the Azolla- and fish-meal-derived fertilizer. These findings indicate that agricultural residues can be converted into liquid fertilizers and that fertilizer formulation and rice variety should be considered together to support rice production.
